compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

A session that holds a ticket `in_progress` learns nothing when another session comments on it, edits it, closes it, or re-claims it after bouncing it to `open` (`claim_core` rejects any non-open ticket, `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:463-475`, so a takeover is always `in_progress → open → claim`, visible as `claimed_session` flipping). No target harness delivers server-initiated MCP notifications into a model's context, so the only reliable channel is the next tracker interaction on whichever seam the session uses. Depends on the MCP identity child [rebar:ffb6-9577-41c3-4c76] for the acting identity over MCP.

## Approach

Add an **inbox**: a per-session, at-most-once feed computed at read time from the event log and delivered on all three seams.

- **Watch list + cursor**, one JSON file per session identity under the existing local-state root `<repo>/.rebar/inbox/<fingerprint>.json` (same root as the `current_session_log` pointer, `src/rebar/_commands/session_log.py:8-38`; git-ignored; the MCP server uses its own checkout's `.rebar`, so a container swap resets the cursor to "last 24h" and re-delivers at most that window once). Fields: `watched_tickets` (added by `claim` when a session identity resolves via `resolve_session_id()`, removed when this session exits `in_progress`), `subscribed_tags`, `position` (an event position `{timestamp}-{uuid}`, the filename prefix `docs/event-schema.md` defines), `last_computed_at`.
- **Producers** (pure functions over the store; rate-limited to one computation per `inbox.min_interval_secs`, default 60, config key modelled on `ensure.hint_interval_secs` at `src/rebar/_config_schema.py:645`): (1) for each watched ticket, event files newer than `position` not authored by this identity → items with `reason ∈ {comment, edit, status_change, claim_lost, closed, link, tag, child_status}`; `claim_lost` fires once when the ticket's `claimed_session` is neither this identity nor null-with-status-in_progress-by-us, and the ticket leaves the watch list; `child_status` covers direct children's status changes for an epic/story holder. (2) tickets created since `position` carrying a subscribed tag → `reason: subscribed_ticket_filed`. The `reason` vocabulary is a formal enum in `inbox.schema.json` so later children (notices, alerts) extend it, not prose.
- **Rendering**: one line per item — `[rebar inbox] <reason> on <alias> by <actor> (<age>) — rebar show <alias>` — never any comment or description text (other agents' prose must not enter a model's context through this channel). Hard caps: 20 lines / 2048 bytes, overflow closed by `+N more — rebar inbox`. Delivery advances the cursor; `--peek` does not.
- **Seams**: MCP — a `read_inbox` tool, `subscribe_inbox`/`unsubscribe_inbox` tools, and a registrar-proxy wrapper (the exact pattern of `suppress_library_double_advisory`, `src/rebar/_lib_warn.py`, applied at `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:674-681`) that, when the feed is non-empty, returns a `CallToolResult` with the tool's original JSON text block plus one appended inbox `TextContent`, `structuredContent` unchanged — `mcp` 1.29.0 re-validates a returned `CallToolResult.structuredContent` against the declared output model (`mcp/server/fastmcp/utilities/func_metadata.py` `convert_result`) and the lowlevel `Server.call_tool` accepts it, so no existing `outputSchema` changes. The block is added after `_mcp_budget` bounding and is capped independently. CLI — `rebar inbox [--peek] [--output json]`, `rebar inbox subscribe|unsubscribe <tag>`, and the same lines on **stderr** after any other command (stdout and exit code untouched; `inbox.enabled = false` silences). Library — `rebar.inbox(peek=False)`, `rebar.subscribe(tag)`, `rebar.unsubscribe(tag)`; single-ticket library writes emit a `RebarInboxWarning` (stdlib `warnings`) through the same guarded emitter shape as `emit_cross_session_warning`.

Positive rationale: read-time producers over the existing event directory naming need no broadcast queue, no new event type, and no commit per delivery; the registrar proxy and `_lib_warn` emitter are proven seams already carrying an advisory today; per-identity watch lists make the feed O(watched tickets) instead of a full-store reduce per call. Default cursor of 24h bounds re-delivery after any state loss.

Failure disposition: any producer error is swallowed and logged at debug (advisory channel, never breaks the primary call), identical to `emit_cross_session_warning`'s contract.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/inbox.py` (new: cursor file, producers, renderer), `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` (claim/transition hooks into the watch list), `src/rebar/_lib_reads.py`/`_lib_writes.py`/`__init__.py` (public API), `src/rebar/_lib_warn.py` (`RebarInboxWarning`).
- `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py`/`_mcp_writes.py`/`_mcp_models.py`/`mcp_server.py` (tools + wrapper), `src/rebar/schemas/inbox.schema.json`, `schemas/__init__.py`, `types.py` (regen), `docs/output-schemas.md`, `docs/mcp-reference.md` (regen), `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py`, `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json` (regen).
- `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/reads.py`, `_cli/_registry.py`, `_cli/_execute.py` (stderr hook), `docs/cli-reference.md` (regen).
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`, `_config_sections.py`, `docs/config-reference.md` (`inbox.enabled`, `inbox.min_interval_secs`, each with a `# mechanism-ok:` marker).
- Consumer scan (T13): every test asserting a single content block on an MCP result (grep `\.content\[0\]` and `len(.*\.content)` under `tests/interfaces/facades/`) is migrated to assert on `structuredContent` or the first block.
- `docs/user-guide.md`, `docs/concurrency.md` (holder-side companion to the actor-side warning).

## Testing

- Unit: producers on a synthetic store — comment/edit/status/link/tag/child_status items, self-authored events excluded (contrast), `claim_lost` fires exactly once and unwatches, cursor advances on deliver and not on peek, caps and overflow line, rate-limit window.
- CLI subprocess: `rebar claim` then a second `REBAR_SESSION_ID` commenting → the first session's next `rebar show` prints the line on stderr, stdout JSON byte-identical to the no-inbox run, exit 0; `inbox.enabled=false` → silent (config-effect contrast).
- MCP in-process client: `claim_ticket` under identity A, `comment_ticket` under B → A's next `list_tickets` result carries a second `TextContent` and its `structuredContent` still validates against the output model; B's result carries none; `subscribe_inbox("x")` then a ticket created with tag `x` → `subscribed_ticket_filed`.
- Library: `rebar.inbox()` returns typed items; `RebarInboxWarning` emitted once, suppressed under the MCP registrar. Gate: `make test`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After session B comments on a ticket session A claimed, A's next tracker call on each seam yields exactly one `comment` item naming B, and A's following call yields none; verified by the three seam tests above.
- [ ] Bouncing A's ticket to `open` and re-claiming it as B yields A exactly one `claim_lost` item and the ticket leaves A's watch list; verified by the unit and MCP tests.
- [ ] No inbox line ever contains comment or description text; verified by a unit test rendering an item whose source comment contains a sentinel string and asserting its absence.
- [ ] The appended MCP block never changes `structuredContent`: every tool in `test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py` still validates with a non-empty feed injected; verified by that test parametrised over feed-present/absent.
- [ ] A session subscribed to tag `ops-alert` receives `subscribed_ticket_filed` for a new ticket carrying it and an unsubscribed session does not; verified by the MCP contrast test.
- [ ] `rebar inbox --output json` validates against `inbox.schema.json`; verified by the schema coverage test.
